journal_lines: §aGravel pocket in the stone. §oThe smell of old riverbed, grit and wet clay.§o §lFlint§l among it. Good pieces.
§aChert nodules in the limestone. Dark, dense, unmistakable by touch.
§aFlint. Sharp edges, solid cores. Kept the best ones.
§aWorked through a gravel seam for an hour. §lFlint§l in the lower half, well-formed.
§aBlack knots in the grey stone. §oFelt them before I saw them in the torchlight.§o Flint.
§aStruck two together out of habit. Spark. Good sign. Kept both.
§aGravel slope at the tunnel base. Sorted through it. Found §lflint§l worth carrying.
§aSurface deposit, loose and easy. Picked out a dozen clean pieces.
§aFound a large nodule and broke it down. §oEach piece sharp as the first.§o Good flint throughout.
§aChipped flint leaves a smell like struck stone. Worked fast. Kept the smell on the paws.
§aQuick work. §lFlint§l near the surface, no deep digging needed.
§aTook only the sharp ones. Left the round ones for the next rain to sort out.
